items.title: Stolen Renoir paintings found behind wall in France
items.summary: PARIS: Two paintings by impressionist master Pierre-Auguste Renoir, stolen from a museum in southern France and later discovered hidden behind a wall, have sustained slight damage, prosecutors said on Monday. The discovery of the stolen works followed the arrest of six people, including a woman, last Wednesday, said Bessone. They were completely undetectable," Bessone said.

items.title: Influencers should not exploit 3R issues for social media content - Yuneswaran
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Social media influencers have been reminded not to exploit issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), particularly religious rituals, for online content, in the interest of preserving harmony in the country's multiracial society. Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said influencers with large followings should be more responsible in producing content and spreading positive values instead of playing on 3R sentiments. Yuneswaran said the ministry viewed the issue involving religious rituals seriously and hoped it would be handled tactfully, adding that the investigation had been left entirely to the religious authorities and the police.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Govt confident of RM510bil expenditure without introducing new taxes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is confident it can fund the RM510 billion expenditure under the 2027 Budget without introducing new taxes, says Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said the government was prioritising better governance to curb leakages and wastage, and improve the efficiency of public spending. Amir Hamzah said Malaysia's strengthening economic data reflected foreign investors' confidence in the country, which could help generate national income.

items.title: Nepal rescuers search for missing after flash flood
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched for five missing people on Monday, a day after devastating flash floods swept away more than 200 houses and five bridges along the Budhi Gandaki river. Videos showed a dark, debris-filled river surging through the hills in central Nepal's Gorkha district. On Sunday, 95 people including nine foreigners were rescued.

items.title: MoH to recommend permanent posts for contract dental, pharmacy officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry (MoH) will recommend absorbing contract dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions for the consideration Finance Ministry and the cabinet. He said the recruitment of dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions would utilise a new quota separate from the 9,000 permanent medical doctor positions announced under the 2027 Budget. The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) previously have urged the government and MoH to consider permanent appointments for contract dental officers, following the announcement of permanent appointments for medical doctors.

items.title: Indonesia rules out national disaster status for forest fires for now
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia will not declare its prolonged forest and land fires a national disaster for now, saying it remains capable of managing the crisis despite concerns over transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia. Dudung said offers of international assistance were not discussed, although he acknowledged concerns from neighbouring countries over the haze. Meanwhile, Dudung said Prabowo had directed firefighting efforts to focus on Tanjung Puting National Park and other affected areas in Central Kalimantan, as well as South Sumatra.

items.title: Sinkhole-prone areas must be assessed before development approval, says ministry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Technical assessments and inspections of aging utilities in sinkhole-prone areas must be conducted before local authorities approve any development, the Housing and Local Government Ministry said. The ministry said the decision was made at the 51st National Physical Planning Council (NPPC) meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. It also approved the Fifth National Physical Plan (RFN5) and the Third National Urbanisation Policy (DPN3) as strategic frameworks for the country's physical and urban development.

items.title: NST Leader: Disaster alert system faces litmus test, success hinges on public response
items.summary: Don't be alarmed: the message is a test from the Cell Broadcast System (CBS), a national disaster warning system that is undergoing pilot testing. Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, the CBS transmits disaster alerts directly to handphones in affected areas. Circumventing handphone numbers, SMS or Internet connection, the CBS will soon replace the existing SMS-based disaster warning system to provide faster and precise alerts.

items.title: Five Malaysians held in Japan over RM3.1mil cocaine haul hidden in shoes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four men and a woman from Malaysia have been arrested at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, Japan, for attempting to smuggle about 5kg of cocaine worth 120 million yen (RM3.1 million), hidden beneath shoe insoles, on Saturday. An initial inspection found cocaine hidden beneath the insoles of two suspects, prompting officers to identify three others believed to have travelled with them. Tokyo Reporter, citing Nippon News Network (NNN), reported that the three others had also concealed cocaine using the same method.

items.title: Man from KL dies after falling from Penang mall car park
items.summary: Northeast district police received a report about the incident around 9.10pm. A witness reportedly saw the man fall from the car park. Northeast district deputy police chief Superintendent Lee Swee Sake confirmed the incident.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Sunday, Oct 12, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1554036]] [[nid:1554035]] [[nid:1554034]] [[nid:1554033]] [[nid:1554032]] [[nid:1554031]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia seeks foreign expertise to unlock RM747bil rare earth potential
items.summary: Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said strategic partnerships with technologically advanced countries were needed to strengthen Malaysia's rare earth processing and manufacturing capabilities, particularly in high-value industries. He said Malaysia had an estimated 16.2 million tonnes of non-radioactive rare earth resources, with industry development expected to create 4,000 jobs. Citing existing investments, Johari said Australian-owned Lynas Malaysia Sdn Bhd had operated a rare earth processing facility in Gebeng, Pahang, since 2012.

items.title: Iron and steel sector faces pressure from dumped imports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The iron and steel sector is among the industries most frequently affected by dumped imports, with the government investigating products from six countries and territories to protect local manufacturers from unfair trade practices. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the investigations covered imports from China, Taipei, South Korea, Japan, India and Vietnam. Malaysia's total imports rose 22.4 per cent to RM1.158 trillion from January to August 2026, while imports from China increased 41.2 per cent to RM308.12 billion, accounting for 21.1 per cent of total imports.

items.title: Search for man swept away in Kajang river suspended due to heavy rain
items.summary: KAJANG: The search and rescue operation for a man believed to have been swept away by river currents in Sungai Chuah yesterday was suspended this afternoon following heavy rain. He said firefighters from the Kajang Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene six minutes later and immediately launched a search for the missing man. "The search and rescue operation will resume tomorrow," he said.

items.title: Takaichi's fiscal shift faces market test
items.summary: Takaichi vowed to cap new debt issuance around 40 trillion yen, even as spending requests for next year's budget hit a record 143 trillion yen. A planned two-year sales tax cut would also cost roughly 4 trillion yen per year. "It's not that market players misunderstand Takaichi's policies.

items.title: Vance 2028 buzz growing, but midterms could sting
items.summary: THE message was clear as United States Vice-President JD Vance shook hands in his native Ohio with a woman wearing a "Vance 2028" cap — at least from his supporter's perspective. "Man, it feels good to be home," Vance said to cheers. There's just one problem for Vance: the midterms themselves.

items.title: Cybercrime Act expected to come into force in early 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Cybercrime Act is expected to come into force in early 2027 as the government steps up efforts to tackle increasingly complex and organised online scams. "The legal framework on cybercrime has also been strengthened through the introduction of the Cybercrime Bill, in line with technological developments and the changing landscape of cybercrime threats. Saifuddin said the Home Ministry would continue to review existing laws to ensure they remained relevant and effective in addressing evolving cybercrime threats.

items.title: 'Ziad's body was smoking': Cousin recounts lightning strike that killed Pasir Mas student
items.summary: "When the lightning struck, all four of us fell backwards, and at that moment, I saw Ziad's body smoking," said Haziq Qayyum Rosli, 12. Haziq is the cousin of Muhammad Ziad Zikri Abdul Hadi, who was killed in the incident. "At that moment (when lightning striked), I saw Ziad's body smoking, and we ran home to inform Ziad's father," he said when met here.

items.title: Wan Rosdy advises Pahang residents to take precautions as haze worsens
items.summary: Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said high-risk groups, including children, the elderly and those with respiratory problems, should take extra precautions. "Parents and event organisers must take appropriate measures to minimise exposure to unhealthy air. Wan Rosdy said he was aware that the Pahang Education Department had ordered schools in Kuantan and Rompin to close tomorrow due to worsening haze and prevailing Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.

items.title: University student, retired engineer lose over RM690,000 to scams in Pahang
items.summary: Acting Bentong police chief Deputy Superintendent Azmi Mahmod said the 18-year-old victim handed over cash and jewellery worth more than RM32,000 to a woman near a supermarket in Karak, Bentong. Azmi said the victim handed the items to a masked woman and was told not to inform his family or anyone else. He said police arrested a 21-year-old local woman near the supermarket around 6.20pm last Saturday.

items.title: Father rushes to paddy field, finds son dead after lightning strike in Pasir Mas [WATCH]
items.summary: "When I was told that Ziad had been struck by lightning, I rushed to the paddy field and cradled him, but my son was already dead," said Abdul Hadi Abdul Ghani, 60. His son, Muhammad Ziad Zikri, a Form Two student, was killed by lightning while fishing at a paddy field in Kampung Tasek Berangan at 4.30pm today. "I cradled Ziad, but he was already gone.

items.title: Foreigner filmed couple, threatened woman before raping her inside mall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down a foreigner, believed to be a Bangladeshi, who allegedly raped a woman on the seventh floor of a shopping centre near Jalan Cochrane here. The suspect reportedly filmed the couple and threatened to circulate the footage if the woman refused to follow his instructions. He then ordered the woman's boyfriend to leave before raping her.

items.title: Foetus found at rubbish disposal site in One Selayang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A foetus believed to be about 24 weeks old was found at a rubbish disposal site in Jalan OS 1/4, One Selayang, Batu Caves, yesterday. Gombak police chief Assistant Commissioner Ibrahim Husin said members of the public alerted police to the discovery at 7.20 pm. Ibrahim urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Gombak police headquarters control centre at 03-6126 2222, investigating officer Inspector Prakash Sithambaram on 012-294 0827, or their nearest police station.

items.title: Malaysia, Jordan explore high-tech cooperation to develop engineers – Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Jordan are exploring stronger cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs. Anwar said the talks also covered cooperation in higher education, skilled human capital development, emerging technologies and the semiconductor ecosystem. Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.

items.title: Semantan Estate files new suit seeking sale of RM13bil Duta Enclave land
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd and its liquidator have filed a new suit in the High Court here against the government and six other defendants over the Duta Enclave land in Kuala Lumpur. They are seeking an order compelling the government to sell the land and account for the proceeds or, alternatively, pay equitable compensation. Semantan Estate claimed that the government took possession of the land between 1956 and 1958 under the Land Acquisition Enactment 1923 for the stated purpose of establishing a "Diplomatic Enclave".

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 12, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Haze school closures. Hit-and-run driver tracked. Zara's mother worried.

items.title: Construction worker jailed three years for abducting, confining Palestinian man
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A construction worker was sentenced to three years' imprisonment by the High Court here today for abducting and confining a Palestinian man at a chalet four years ago. Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin imposed the sentence on Edy Ko'im Said, 46, after he pleaded guilty to an alternative charge. They are Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45, Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45, Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46, Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60, Nidarahayu Zainal, 40, and Raibafie Amdan, 45.

items.title: Retaining wall collapses after heavy rain, damaging six vehicles in Kajang [WATCH]
items.summary: The incident, which occurred around 5pm, damaged three cars and three motorcycles when soil came crashing down onto the vehicles. Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations indicated that the retaining wall had failed to withstand soil movement following heavy rain that began around 3pm. "The collapse caused soil to fall onto several vehicles parked near the affected area," he said in a statement.

items.title: Federal-state cooperation key to sustainable development, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Close cooperation between the federal and state governments is key to ensuring inclusive and sustainable national development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post, Anwar said this while chairing the 51st National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) meeting in Putrajaya today. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the meeting reviewed various aspects of national physical development, including land-use planning and state structure plans, in accordance with the Town and Country Planning Act .

items.title: Boy, 7, injured in stray dog attack in Lima Kedai
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A 7-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by a pack of six to eight stray dogs while playing at a playground near a low-cost flat in Lima Kedai here today. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the incident occurred between 3pm and 4pm, when the boy was playing in the area before the dogs attacked him, causing him to fall and roll on the ground as he tried to escape. he said.

items.title: Firefly cancels Subang-Singapore flights until October 14 as haze persists
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Oct 12 — Prevailing weather and haze conditions have forced Firefly to extend flight cancellations between Subang and Singapore’s Seletar Airport until October 14, with affected passengers being offered alternative Malaysia Airlines flights, subject to seat availability, or full refunds. Firefly, a wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia Airlines, had earlier cancelled all scheduled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Seletar Airport from October 10 to 12 as a precautionary safety measure. “Affected passengers are being contacted and reallocated onto available Malaysia Airlines services via the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore route, subject to seat availability.

items.title: Federal-state cooperation key to inclusive, sustainable development, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Close cooperation between the federal and state governments is essential to ensuring that national development is planned in an inclusive, sustainable and comprehensive manner for the benefit of the people. In a Facebook post, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he made the remarks while chairing the 51st National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) meeting in Putrajaya today. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the meeting reviewed various matters related to national physical development, including land-use planning and State Structure Plans, in line with the Town and Country Planning Act 1976 (Act 172).

items.title: Kedah police: Motorcycle theft allegation believed to have led to teen’s torture death
items.summary: Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said police received information about the discovery of the body at 8.05am on October 8, while a post-mortem found that the victim had died from blunt force trauma to the head. Adzli said the victim was found dead inside the house on the night of October 7, and his body was subsequently dumped by the roadside. Police seized 14 mobile phones, a Honda City, scissors and the victim’s identity card.

items.title: Finance Ministry to strengthen oversight of public funds through amended Audit Act, new procurement law
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Finance Ministry will use amendments to the Audit Act 1957 and the Government Procurement Act 2026 to strengthen oversight of public funds and improve transparency in government spending. Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the amended Audit Act gives the Auditor-General greater scope to trace funds across government agencies and examine how the money is used. “The government has also approved the Government Procurement Act, which enables the government to tighten oversight in terms of transparency and value for money in the procurement process.

items.title: Malaysia targets 3.3pc fiscal deficit in 2027, 3pc by 2028, says Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Malaysia is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent next year as it presses ahead with plans to bring the figure down to 3 per cent by 2028, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said today. Speaking at a panel discussion titled “Post-Budget 2027 Debate” organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur, Johan said fiscal consolidation remained a key government priority, particularly in maintaining investor confidence. The government is targeting a fiscal deficit of 3.6 per cent this year, after reducing it from 5.5 per cent in 2022 to 3.7 per cent in 2025.

items.title: Seven-year-old seriously injured in Johor stray dog attack, teen escapes unhurt in earlier incident at same location
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 12 — A seven-year-old boy suffered serious injuries after he was attacked by eight stray dogs while playing at a playground at a housing complex in Lima Kedai here today. Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad expressed concern over the incident urging authorities to address the issue of stray dogs. Pandak said the incident involving the child was the second to occur today.

items.title: Govt aims to improve water quality in 33 polluted rivers in Malaysia by 10pc, says DPM Fadillah
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the target was set at the second 2026 meeting of the National Special Committee on Addressing River Water Quality Deterioration, which he chaired today. In Selangor, the Selangor Water Management Authority (Luas) reported 144 cases of water source pollution detected over the three years up to September 14, 2026, with varying levels of risk. Fadillah said polluted rivers could disrupt water treatment plant operations, affect public water supplies, increase treatment costs and affect economic activities, underscoring the need to make water resource protection a shared priority at all levels of administration.

items.title: Budget 2027: Pet vaccination, sterilisation eligible for tax relief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The government proposes expanding the scope of individual income tax relief for lifestyle to include pet care expenses, such as vaccinations and sterilisation treatments by registered veterinary services. MoF said the personal income tax relief cap for lifestyle remains at RM2,500, including the proposed expansion. Additionally, to promote digital literacy and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology to boost productivity and drive innovation, the scope of the personal income tax relief for lifestyle is proposed to be expanded to include subscription costs for AI software and applications for personal use, spouses, or children.

items.title: High Court allows MCMC’s preliminary objection, Papagomo committal hearing on Dec 23
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court will first hear the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) committal application against blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, before proceeding with the inter-partes injunction hearing. “The court also extended the existing ad interim injunction against Wan Muhammad Azri until December 23. Therefore, MCMC has applied to the court for leave to commence a committal proceeding against Wan Azri.

items.title: Malaysia, Jordan seek high-tech cooperation to train more engineers, says Anwar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Malaysia and Jordan are seeking to expand strategic cooperation in high-tech industries, particularly semiconductors and advanced technical education and training, to develop more engineers and skilled workers for future industry needs. “We also discussed potential cooperation in developing advanced technical education and training centres, including producing more engineers and skilled workers to meet future industry demands,” he posted on Facebook. Anwar said discussions also covered expanding trade and investment, including a potential free trade agreement (FTA), tariff restructuring, stronger supply chains and cooperation in energy, transport, the halal industry and tourism.

items.title: TNB confirms electrical accident at its installation in Johor’s Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has confirmed an electrical accident involving a member of the public at one of its installations in Kota Tinggi, Johor, today. In a statement posted on Facebook by TNB CareLine, the utility company said its technical team was dispatched to the location shortly after receiving a report of the incident. The company also advised the public against tampering with, opening or approaching electrical installations, warning that such actions could result in serious injury or death.

items.title: No need to replace old birth certificates, still valid, says NRD; new copies cost RM5
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 12 — Old birth certificates, including handwritten documents issued in paper format, remain valid and do not need to be replaced, said National Registration Department (NRD) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias. Badrul Hisham said birth documentation was essential to establish a legally recognised identity and ensure individuals could access their rights and services as Malaysians. He said the NRD continued to reach out to communities, including the Orang Asli in rural areas, to ensure they had access to registration and documentation services.

items.title: Kedah police bust online scam syndicate posing as Indian police officers
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 12 — Kedah police successfully crippled an online scam syndicate involving suspects posing as Indian police officers during a raid on a business premises in Bandar Putra, Kulim, last Friday. Kedah Police Chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said that during the joint operation at 8pm, police arrested 48 individuals suspected of acting as syndicate members, comprising seven locals, eight Indian nationals, and 33 Pakistani nationals. “Additionally, police seized various items including 89 mobile phones, seven laptops, modems, monitors, Indian police uniforms, Indian flags, Indian Central Bureau of Investigation flags, and several other items.

items.title: Two killed, two injured in three-vehicle pile-up on Federal Highway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two men were killed while two others were injured in an accident involving three cars at Kilometer 18.2 of the Federal Highway heading towards Kuala Lumpur, early this morning. Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said the accident, which occurred at approximately 12.20am, involved a Proton Wira driven by a local man in his 20s who was travelling from Shah Alam to Kuala Lumpur. Shamsudin said the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters received a report regarding the fatal accident at 1:05 am today.

items.title: Opposition leader criticises GLC involvement in non-core projects in Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that government-linked corporations (GLCs) were being made to operate beyond their core mandates. While debating Budget 2027, he cited a project to build a hostel for students that he said would be funded by the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP), alleging this practice extended to others such as Petronas, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and more. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for 2027 last Friday, in which he also outlined a RM50 billion from government-linked investment companies, state enterprises and statutory bodies.

items.title: 1MDB in talks to settle lawsuit with Deutsche Bank
items.summary: 1MDB’s counsel, Datuk Lim Chee Wee, informed the Federal Court of the settlement talks during proceedings today before a three-member panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah. The panel, comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Seri Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru, was hearing 1MDB’s application for leave to appeal against a decision in favour of UK law firm White & Case LLP. The hearing for that case is scheduled for October 26 before High Court Judicial Commissioner Rihada Rafie,” Lim said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan ruler to skip Conference of Rulers meeting, palace says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, will not attend the Conference of Rulers meeting scheduled from October 13 to 15, the Negeri Sembilan Palace said today. In a statement, Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said attendance at the Conference of Rulers meeting did not require an invitation. He also clarified that Tuanku Muhriz had not received any letter or formal invitation from the meeting’s chairman, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah, to attend the pre-council meeting.

items.title: High Court jails construction worker three years for Palestinian abduction tied to hacking secrets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — A construction worker who was previously charged with kidnapping a Palestinian man was sentenced to three years in prison by the High Court here today for abducting and confining the man at a chalet four years ago. Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin imposed the sentence on Edy Ko’im Said, 46, after he pleaded guilty to an alternative charge of abducting and confining the Palestinian man. The court ordered the father of three to begin serving his prison sentence today.

items.title: Batik Air: Flight OD701 from KLIA to Jeddah called off as precautionary measure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Batik Air has cancelled its scheduled flight from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, today as a precautionary measure amid the ongoing conflict. “The affected flight, OD701, was scheduled to depart Kuala Lumpur for King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah at 7.25pm. Passengers were also advised to check Batik Air’s official website and social media channels for the latest flight updates.

items.title: Haze worsens: 23 stations record ‘Unhealthy’ API levels across Malaysia
items.summary: No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels. Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the highest reading at 174, followed by Kota Tinggi, also in Johor, at 170. Johor had seven stations in the unhealthy range.

items.title: Kuraman Island sand spit stretches into record books, spurring Labuan’s ecotourism appeal
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 12 — The natural sand spit on Kuraman Island has set two national records in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBR), with its total length measuring 808.4 metres and its exposed section measuring 790.4 metres. The two records are ‘Longest Natural Sand Spit in Malaysia’ (Beting Pasir Semula Jadi Terpanjang di Malaysia) and ‘Longest Exposed Sand Spit in Malaysia’ (Beting Pasir Terdedah Terpanjang di Malaysia). Muhammad Azmi said the recognition marked a significant milestone in efforts to promote Labuan’s geological heritage and tourism potential, while raising the profile of Kuraman Island and Labuan Geopark nationally.

items.title: Fadhlina: Schools closed tomorrow in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Putrajaya as haze worsens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Schools across Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, and Putrajaya, as well as several districts in Selangor and Pahang, will be closed tomorrow following a sharp deterioration in air quality, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today. The mandatory closures also extend to schools under four District Education Offices (PPD) in Selangor: Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat, and Sepang. In Pahang, schools under PPD Kuantan and PPD Rompin will likewise remain closed.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh says DBKL, police mull joint control centre for KL’s 10,000 CCTVs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) are considering establishing a control centre to give the police better access to the closed-circuit television (CCTV) system across the federal capital. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the initiative is crucial as about 10,000 CCTV units are installed throughout Kuala Lumpur. Sentul police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the ICT system will significantly help speed up services to the public, especially when lodging police reports.

items.title: Education minister: Decisions on school haze closures guided by MetMalaysia, Health Ministry and NRES
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Decisions regarding the closure and reopening of schools due to the haze situation will be made periodically based on standard operating procedures (SOPs), existing guidelines, and advice from relevant agencies. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said these decisions depend on advice of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) and the Ministry of Health (MOH), as well as the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES). Fadhlina said the current haze situation is being monitored according to established guidelines, however, parents must continue to prioritise their children’s health.

items.title: High Court fixes June 14, 2027 for Bar bid to revive Zahid graft case
items.summary: Judge S. Indra Nehru set the date after lawyer Abhilaash Subramaniam, representing the Malaysian Bar, informed the court that Ahmad Zahid and the Attorney-General (AG) had obtained leave from the Federal Court on Oct 8 to appeal against an earlier Court of Appeal ruling. “We therefore request that the judicial review hearing at the High Court be held after the Federal Court appeal proceedings are concluded,” Abhilaash said during case management. The court also directed that the next case management be conducted via e-review before a High Court deputy registrar.

items.title: Opposition leader challenges Putrajaya to revive GST, end ‘uncertainty’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that the government’s hybrid taxation proposal was tacit admission that it was wrong to reject the goods and services tax (GST). While debating the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027, Hamzah said recent proposals to incorporate elements of the consumption tax into the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) also indicated that the latter system was lacking. “If you want the GST, just implement the GST.

items.title: Malaysia urges Umrah pilgrims to hold off travel after deadly Riyadh airport missile strike
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 12 — Malaysians are advised to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. “There has been no incident in Makkah, but the missile explosion in Riyadh has raised security concerns,” he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan’s King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here today Yesterday, the Foreign Ministry reported that no Malaysians had been killed or injured in Saturday’s attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh or the incident involving a projectile that fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that the attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309 others.

items.title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across nine states, Putrajaya and Labuan until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across multiple states, forecasting heavy rain, lightning, and gusty winds in parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, Sabah, and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today. In the northern and eastern regions of the peninsula, the warning encompasses Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, and Selama), Kelantan (Jeli and Gua Musang), and Terengganu (Dungun, Hulu Terengganu, and Kemaman). In Negeri Sembilan, stormy weather is expected across Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, and Kuala Pilah.

items.title: Man found electrocuted beside Kota Tinggi TNB substation, cable theft attempt suspected
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 12 — An unidentified man was found dead early this morning, believed to have been electrocuted while attempting to steal power cables near a Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) substation in Felda Adela, near Sungai Rengit. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said law enforcement was alerted after receiving an emergency call through the MERS 999 response system at 6.46am regarding an unconscious individual. “Following the information, a police team from the Kota Tinggi district police headquarters were immediately despatched to the scene to investigate.

items.title: From Jan 2027, only JPJ‑approved intermediaries can handle customer transactions at counters nationwide
items.summary: ARAU, Oct 12 — Only individuals or company representatives registered as intermediaries and approved by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) will be allowed to conduct transactions on behalf of customers at all JPJ offices and branches nationwide from January 1. JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the requirement was aimed at regulating intermediary services more systematically, transparently and with integrity. Aedy Fadly said the implementation did not mean that JPJ had any ties, cooperation or business relationship with any registered intermediary.
